newsitem.title: PANAMA: Panama's cabinet reshuffled, new finance minister.
newsitem.headline: Panama's cabinet reshuffled, new finance minister.

text.p: Panamana's President Ernesto Perez Balladares slightly reshuffled his cabinet Monday and named a new Finance Minister in what political sources saw as a move to put more close political allies in key positions.

In the first cabinet changes since he took office in September 1994, the Panamanian leader named Finance and Treasury Minister Olmedo Miranda to the key post of Minister of the Presidency, a presidential spokesman said.
Miranda's replacement was his former deputy Miguel Heras.
Raul Arango, previously Minister of the Presidency, moved to the Commerce ministry where he will replace Nitzia de Villarreal whose new job has yet to be announced, the spokesman said.
No official reason was given for the reshuffle but political sources said Perez Balladares wanted to shore up support within the ruling Democratic Revolutionary Party (PRD).
"The changes were made to consolidate party support. He's preparing for the 1999 elections," one source said.

"Miranda is a close, personal friend. The president wanted to have a close friend in the presidency," the source added. Arango was put in charge of trade "because he is a close friend of the business community."
